newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile to speed up negotiated bid process.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile to speed up negotiated bid process.

text.p: The Defense National Stockpile Center said it will change the way it handles negotiated sales in order to speed up the process following trader unease over the recent cobalt sale.

"The market has been consistently telling me our process takes too long. We are working on ways to shorten it, and within the next month we will come up with some kind of changes," Stockpile administrator Richard Connelly said.
There was some disgruntlement that bidders were asked to submit a second round of "best and final" offers.
However, the principle of a negotiated sale would be kept, Connelly added.
The latest negotiated cobalt sale was concluded Tuesday with 1.1 million pounds of metal awarded. The bids had been with the Stockpile since February 20.
Leaving bids open for a month in a volatile market like cobalt was too long, some traders have said.
The next negotiated bid for cobalt will be in April, with a further 1 million pounds on offer.
A million pounds of cobalt will also be offered on a sealed bid basis March 31.
Last week trader Minor Metals Inc protested to the U.S. General Accounting Office, accusing the Stockpile of potentially revealing the company's trade secrets to other cobalt bidders.
No other bidder made any official protests, Connelly said.

"I have never seen any evidence whatsoever that anybody's trade secrets have been released," Connelly said. "I am confident it did not happen. I could not be more comfortable that any investigation will show my staff handled themselves professionally."
"We certainly made sure we had authority to do so (make the award Tuesday) before we did," Connelly added.
